name: Polycystic Kidney Disease, Autosomal Recessive

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys with poor corticomedullary differentiation on ultrasound
Evidence of congenital hepatic fibrosis or portal hypertension
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the PKHD1 gene
Consanguinity or family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys on imaging plus identification of biallelic PKHD1 pathogenic variants or clinical features consistent with ARPKD in infancy/early childhood
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory; imaging findings are critical for early diagnosis.

searchTerms: both kidneys enlarged and bright on ultrasound
bilateral kidney swelling with abnormal texture

pathognomonic.notes: Considered part of the hepatobiliary system but classified under constitutional for this profile
searchTerms: fibrous liver tissue present at birth

common.symptomName: Hypertension in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: high blood pressure in babies or young children

common.symptomName: Impaired renal function progressing to chronic kidney disease

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to pulmonary hypoplasia
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to lung underdevelopment
poor lung growth causing breathing problems

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal impairment
Elevated liver enzymes in cases with hepatic fibrosis
imaging: Ultrasound showing bilaterally enlarged echogenic kidneys with poor corticomedullary differentiation
MRI or CT demonstrating hepatic fibrosis and portal hypertension
Chest X-ray showing pulmonary hypoplasia in neonates
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in PKHD1 gene
other: Histopathology of liver biopsy showing congenital hepatic fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple renal cysts with normal kidney size initially
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress in neonate due to pulmonary hypoplasia
Rapidly progressive renal failure in infancy
Signs of portal hypertension such as gastrointestinal bleeding
references: Harris PC, Torres VE. Polycystic kidney disease. Annu Rev Med. 2009;60:321-37.
Guay-Woodford LM. Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease: the clinical experience in North America. Pediatr Nephrol. 2003;18(9): 863-868.
